summary: Researched the foundation for the /sapience command: verified all dispatch-cited mechanisms (project-share route, ownership/cross-door semantics, repo_link.py's exact file format, credential precedence, the write-path rule, and the dead REPO_LINK_FOR path) directly against primary sources, and surfaced an implementation-facing tension between this task's new scripts/lib/sapience-api-lib.sh and the extension's prior per-script-duplication convention, plus the need to extend test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh's lockstep-guard file list.

artifacts.summary: Confirms the dispatch's technical claims against brain_server.py, repo_link.py, and ~/.sapience/mcp.py; documents the extension's existing scripts/lib absence, the lockstep worktree-resolution test's hardcoded five-file list, and recommends the shared lib's exact helper surface and output-envelope contract for the vault-read script.

memory_candidates.content: Deploy flattens every extension's scripts/ tree into one shared .claude/scripts/ directory, and every extension's own scripts/lib/ entries land in one shared .claude/scripts/lib/ -- not a per-extension subdirectory. Confirmed via .claude-extensions.json's installed_files for the sapience extension (every script lands at .claude/scripts/<name>.sh) and via core's deploy-headless.sh/verify-deploy.sh comments, which all target one .claude/scripts/lib/ regardless of source extension. A new lib filename from any extension only needs to avoid collision with every OTHER extension's lib filenames, not just its own.

agent-system/extensions/sapience/scripts/tests/test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh Case 30 asserts a marker-delimited worktree-checkout-resolution block is byte-identical across a HARDCODED LOCKSTEP_FILES array of exactly five file paths (the SessionStart hook, verify-sapience-mcp.sh, sapience-retrieve.sh, sapience-remember.sh, verify-sapience-context-scoping.sh). Adding the same marker block to a new script does NOT get covered by this test unless the new path is explicitly appended to that array -- the comparison is not self-discovering across the filesystem.

repo_link.py's parse_link rejects a dict carrying ANY key matching /(token|key|secret|password)/i (re.IGNORECASE), not just the three named project/name/repo keys -- so a committed link file intended for server consumption must carry exactly those three keys and nothing else. Its own canonical serializer link_text() uses json.dumps(..., indent=2, sort_keys=False) plus a trailing newline in the fixed order project, name, repo; a hand-rolled writer that accepts the same object shape but serializes differently (key order, indentation) will still parse correctly today but diverges byte-for-byte from what the server's own writer would produce once the gating flag is enabled.
